findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed. For an empty slice, `samples.iter().sum()` yields 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so the head code computes `0u32 / 0u32`. Rust integer division by zero panics in every build profile, so `average(&[])` panics instead of returning the 0 promised by the doc comment on line 1.

Trigger: Calling average with an empty slice, e.g. average(&[]).

Impact: Any caller that passes an empty slice, which the doc comment says yields 0, now panics. This is a crash on a path the documented contract covers.
findings.suggestion: Restore the guard: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
findings.title: average panics with division by zero on empty input

risk_level.reason: The empty-slice guard was removed, so average() now divides by zero when samples is empty, contradicting its documented return of 0 and causing a panic.
